\\Microsoft\\Windows\\LanguageComponents.title: Language Components Installer
\\Microsoft\\Windows\\LanguageComponents.explanation: Installs pending language features-on-demand (typing, spellcheck, handwriting, OCR, speech) for the user's language list. Runs 15 minutes after each logon and repeats daily until nothing is pending (trigger id 'PeriodicInstallationAfterLogonUntilDone'). A sub-second run ending in return code 0 means nothing was pending - the check itself was the whole visit.
\\Microsoft\\Windows\\LanguageComponents.note: 'Install $(Arg0)' with the placeholder unexpanded is normal: the argument is only substituted when something starts the task with a parameter; a trigger-fired start has none.

\\Microsoft\\Windows\\LanguageComponents.title: Language Resources Reconciliation
\\Microsoft\\Windows\\LanguageComponents.explanation: Reconciles per-user language resources after logon or language-list changes (COM handler 'LanguageOverlayServer'). Routine logon-time housekeeping; return code 0 within a second is the normal outcome.

\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CloudRestore\\Back.title: Windows settings backup (cloud restore)
\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CloudRestore\\Back.explanation: Backs up Windows settings and the Microsoft Store app list for device replacement and recovery scenarios (Windows settings backup). The $(Arg0) placeholder receives the backup payload when the task is invoked with one.

\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Bluetooth\\Uninsta.title: Bluetooth device uninstall
\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Bluetooth\\Uninsta.explanation: Runs BthUdTask.exe to clean up a Bluetooth device; $(Arg0) receives the device identifier when the task is invoked with a parameter.

\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Maps\\MapsToastTas.title: Maps update/toast check
\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Maps\\MapsToastTas.explanation: Checks for Maps data updates and shows related notifications. The $(Arg0)..$(Arg7) placeholders carry invocation parameters and are normally seen unexpanded.

\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Workplace Join\\Au.title: Automatic workplace join
\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Workplace Join\\Au.explanation: Registers the device at logon via dsregcmd (workplace / Microsoft Entra join). Commonly Disabled on home machines - that state is fine.

\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Shell\\FamilySafet.title: Family Safety refresh
\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Shell\\FamilySafet.explanation: Refreshes Microsoft Family Safety settings and activity state for the signed-in user.

\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Flighting\\OneSett.title: OneSettings cache refresh
\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Flighting\\OneSett.explanation: Fetches OneSettings remote config (feature flags, experiment cohorts) as SYSTEM via a COM handler. Stock cadence is a repeating time trigger (~3h20m stock, ~3h36m on current builds) with a 1h random delay plus WNF state-change triggers - roughly 20-40 runs a day. Runs of a second or two ending in return code 0 are normal. The OneSettingsCadence CLI can lower this cadence and restore stock afterwards.
